steps.body: When one fraction equals another, **cross-multiplication** clears both denominators at once: a/b = c/d ⟺ ad = bc. Solve (x + 1)/4 = (x − 2)/2: cross gives 2(x + 1) = 4(x − 2) → 2x + 2 = 4x − 8 → x = **5**.

The classic application: **work rates**. A machine finishing a job in a hours does 1/a of it per hour. Working together, rates ADD: 1/a + 1/b = 1/t, where t is the joint time. Two painters at 6 and 3 hours: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 — together they take **2 hours**.

explanationVariants: Finishing in 4 hours means 1/4 of the job each hour.
Rate is the reciprocal of the completion time.

widget.prompt: A pump fills a tank in 4 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill per hour?

options.feedback: Right — one whole tank spread over 4 hours.
4 is the TIME — the per-hour rate is its reciprocal, 1/4 of a tank.
1/2 per hour would finish in 2 hours — this pump needs 4: rate 1/4.
3/4 is what remains after one hour — the rate is what gets DONE: 1/4.

widget.prompt: Pipes fill a tank alone in 6 hours and 3 hours. Using 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/t, how many hours does t take together?

commonErrors.feedback: Times don't average — RATES add: 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 per hour, so t = 2.
Adding the times ignores teamwork — add the RATES: 1/2 per hour means 2 hours.

explanationVariants: The joint time is always LESS than the fastest solo time — help can only speed things up: t = 2 < 3.
Any t bigger than the best solo time signals an equation slip.

widget.prompt: Two workers finish alone in 6 and 3 hours. Which is a sanity check on their joint time t?

options.label: t must be less than 3
options.feedback: Right — adding a helper can't slow the faster worker; t = 2 passes.

options.label: t must be between 3 and 6
options.feedback: Between the times is where AVERAGING lands you — real teamwork beats the faster solo time.

options.label: t must equal 4.5
options.feedback: 4.5 is the average of the times — rates add, times don't: t = 2.

options.label: t must be more than 6
options.feedback: That would mean the helper HURT — joint work is faster than either alone.

explanationVariants: Clear by 6x if you prefer: x + 6 = 3x → x = 3.

widget.prompt: With a 6-hour machine, the pair finishes in 2 hours: 1/6 + 1/x = 1/2. Solve for x.

numericErrors.feedback: Rates SUBTRACT here, times don't add: 1/x = 1/3, so x = 3.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

widget.prompt: Machines finish alone in 4 hours and 12 hours. How many hours together?

numericErrors.feedback: Times don't average (8 = (4+12)/2) — rates add: 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3, so t = 3.
16 ADDS the times — together is FASTER than either alone: t = 3.

steps.body: Cross-multiply proportions; add RATES (never times) for joint work.
takeaways: a/b = c/d ⟺ ad = bc — one move clears both bottoms.
A t-hour job means a 1/t-per-hour rate.
Joint time beats the fastest solo time — a built-in sanity check.
